### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **64** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-client.mdx`  _(via waitMs (symbol, a field of interface AuditSealLockHoldOptions; a field of interface DatabaseSessionLockWait))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-key-material (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-key-material.ts), os migrate audit-mail-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-mail-bodies.ts), os migrate audit-metadata-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts), os migrate audit-side-copies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-side-copies.ts))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via waitMs (symbol, a field of interface AuditSealLockHoldOptions; a field of interface DatabaseSessionLockWait))_
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-key-material (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-key-material.ts), os migrate audit-side-copies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-side-copies.ts))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-metadata-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-metadata-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-key-material (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-key-material.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-side-copies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-side-copies.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **26** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **58** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `437cc408c7ad731e07ac2091414966087dd7ddce` — the merge of head `972c3ec2625d60e2ef17c62ba11e09a813502d2a` into base `63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 437cc408c7ad731e07ac2091414966087dd7ddce && git checkout 437cc408c7ad731e07ac2091414966087dd7ddce
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728 972c3ec2625d60e2ef17c62ba11e09a813502d2a && git checkout -B drift-repro 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728 && git merge --no-ff 972c3ec2625d60e2ef17c62ba11e09a813502d2a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Expect red in "skips the pass while another session holds it" and "a sealer pass skips while a run holds it". The subject resolves through src, so no dist rebuild is needed.
4. **Full dogfood battery at the final head, not run.** It is owed because the title carries `!`.
5. **Not run either:** the CI check-runs read, the review#3 request once CI is green, and the report file under the area's orders directory.

**Notes.**
- The PR body's Clause-② widened list omits the new plugin-audit export `STORED_METADATA_BODY_REWRITTEN_OBJECTS`, which the changeset does name. That is for the seat to amend; a dev does not PATCH the body.

- The extraction is faithful. `acquireSchemaMigrationLock` now calls `acquireDatabaseSessionLock` with its own name, wait, wait line and refusal; the statements, their order, the bindings, the `55P03` reading, the MySQL seconds rounding, the dialect read before `getKnex()` and the close on every failure are the ones removed from `schema-migration-lock.ts`, and `SCHEMA_MIGRATION_PG_LOCK_KEY` derives through the same expression. Nothing an existing caller sees moves.
- E as ruled, for one database per deployment. The sealer takes `audit.sealer`, then try-locks `objectstack:audit-seal` on each sealed object's hot store, lets go of both and writes nothing when another session holds it, and checks both locks before each checkpoint write. An `--apply` run of each of the four rewrites takes the lock before its first write, hot and archive runs inside the hold, and lets it go after its last; a dry run takes none.
- Both sides agree on where and on what. Each reads `lifecycle.seal` off the engine registry and locks on `engine.getDriverForObject(object)`, so the two always meet on the same database for the same object; archive rows are covered because both sides lock on the hot store. The hold reads a superset of the sealer's plans (an object that declares the seal but cannot be sealed is still locked for), which errs on the safe side.
- The object lists handed to the hold are the lists the rewrites walk: `KEY_MATERIAL_COPY_TABLES`, `MAIL_LOG_BODY_COPY_OBJECTS`, the `--object` selection of the side-copies run, and `STORED_METADATA_BODY_REWRITTEN_OBJECTS`, which the metadata-bodies run now builds its table list from.
- B as ruled. A dialect other than Postgres or MySQL, a driver with no Knex and an object with no driver all answer no lock; the run is then refused before `rewrite` starts unless `--sealer-stopped`, and with the flag it says on whose word it runs. A failure to take the lock on a database that offers one is handed on, never read as no lock (pinned). The red line holds on every path read.
- The ruling's two pins are present: the lock on the hot store and not the primary, for the hold and for the sealer; the wait at ten minutes with a staged sealer pass waited out under the default.
- A lost session is reported: `finish()` probes each lock before releasing it, and each command prints the line and exits non-zero, in JSON mode as `sealLockLost`.

- Declared pair: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, on the PR body and the changeset. Both hold: no schema key, accepted value or metadata type moves; a command run that 18.4.0 performed is now refused in two stated cases, and a flag and exports are added.

- New published names match the barrels: objectql `acquireDatabaseSessionLock`, `tryDatabaseSessionLock`, `databaseSessionLockPgKey` and two types; plugin-audit `holdAuditSealLock`, `AUDIT_SEAL_LOCK_NAME`, `AUDIT_SEAL_LOCK_WAIT_MS`, `STORED_METADATA_BODY_REWRITTEN_OBJECTS` and three types. The changeset names all of them; the PR body does not (N1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: written through the relay.
- Independence: exception — same account (os-elon-musk) implemented this PR; the maintainer ruled 2026-11-15T12:51Z (project thread) that review#1 reviews this account's own drain PRs.
- No new id materialisation or in-app join. The lock adds one dedicated connection per database for the length of each sealer pass and each `--apply` run, outside the pool; a database at its connection limit now fails the pass (closed, and reported) where it sealed before.
- No security boundary is moved.
- CI: every check-run on this head has completed, none red (success or skipped). Readings the dev report lists as not run (the ablation, the full dogfood battery owed by the `!`) are the lane seat's to clear; this record does not stand in for them.

- Tier evidence. `verify-review-tier.mjs` on this reviewer's own transcript passes: every turn served at the tier named above.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself holds against ADR-0154 D3 as amended: it takes away only the run the ADR now refuses, at the commands the ADR names, and makes the red line real where no lock exists. It fails in one supported topology:

- M1 (must-fix) — the lock excludes this process from itself when two sealed objects route to two datasources on one lock namespace. `byDriver` in `seal-lock.ts` groups by driver object and opens one session per driver. A MySQL `GET_LOCK` name is server-wide and a Postgres advisory lock is database-wide, so two datasources on one MySQL server (two schemas, the usual way to split an audit store), or two datasources on one Postgres database, share the lock while holding two sessions. Then `trySealPassLocks` takes the lock on the first driver and reads `held` on the second: every pass is skipped, for good, at `info` once an hour, with a line that blames a migration run or another server. And `holdAuditSealLock` takes the first and waits ten minutes on its own session for the second, then refuses; on these dialects `--sealer-stopped` does not let the run through. `sys_audit_log` and `sys_activity`, the two objects three of the rewrites walk, are exactly the pair an app can seal and route apart. Before this PR that deployment sealed; after it, sealing stops without an error. The PR body notes the server-wide name only across deployments. A fix has to tell "held by a session of this run" from "held by another": for example ask the holder (`pg_locks` against the pids of the sessions this call opened; `IS_USED_LOCK` against their connection ids) before reading a second answer as contention, with a pin on two drivers over one `sessionLockDatabase`.
- N1 (nit) — the PR body's `Clause-②` line names three commands and omits `STORED_METADATA_BODY_REWRITTEN_OBJECTS` and the type names; the changeset is complete. The body is the seat's to amend.
- N2 (nit) — in a run over two databases, the B refusal for the lockless one is thrown only after the wait on the other has ended, up to ten minutes later. Checking for the lockless objects first costs nothing.
- N3 (nit) — `isHeld()` runs `select 1` with no timeout; on a half-open connection the probe, and with it the pass or `finish()`, waits on the transport.
